title: Supply chain disruption on auto manufacturer stocks

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Event-study.

Rationale  
• The semiconductor-shortage announcement is a single, well–defined shock that hit all listed auto manufacturers simultaneously.  
• In efficient markets, any causal price reaction should materialise immediately around the announcement; hence abnormal returns (AR) and cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) in a short window identify the causal effect.  

Key identifying assumptions  
1. No confounding firm-specific or market-wide news occurs in the estimation or event windows (“clean” event).  
2. Market model estimated over the pre-event window [−10,−2] accurately captures the normal (counterfactual) return process.  
3. Semi-strong form market efficiency: prices impound all public information so any abnormal return around day 0 is attributable to the shortage news.  

## 2. R Code
```r
###############################################################################
# Event study: semiconductor shortage and auto stocks
#   – Computes AR and CAR per stock
#   – Cross-sectional regression of CAR on chip dependency
#   – Basic robustness checks
###############################################################################

library(tidyverse)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# 1. Read data ---------------------------------------------------------------
df <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s16_data.csv",
               col_types = cols())

# Quick check for chip-dependency variable name ------------------------------
chip_var <- names(df)[str_detect(names(df), "chip")]
if (length(chip_var) == 0) {
  stop("No chip-dependency variable found in the dataset.")
} else {
  chip_var <- chip_var[1]   # first matching column
}

# 2. Define estimation and event windows -------------------------------------
est_win  <- -10:-2               # estimation window
event_win <- 0:5                 # main event window
event_win_alt <- 0:3             # robustness window

# 3. Estimate alpha & beta and compute AR ------------------------------------
# Helper: function that returns a tibble with AR by stock & day
get_AR <- function(d){
  # estimation
  est <- d %>% filter(event_day %in% est_win)
  fit <- lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = est)

  alpha <- coef(fit)[1]
  beta  <- coef(fit)[2]

  # abnormal returns for all days kept for flexibility
  d %>% 
    mutate(alpha = alpha,
           beta_est = beta,
           AR = ret - (alpha + beta * mkt_ret))
}

df_ar <- df %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  group_modify(~get_AR(.x)) %>% 
  ungroup()

# 4. Obtain CAR per stock -----------------------------------------------------
car_tbl <- df_ar %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% event_win) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  summarise(CAR_0_5 = sum(AR),
            .groups = "drop") %>% 
  # Alternative window for robustness
  left_join(
    df_ar %>% 
      filter(event_day %in% event_win_alt) %>% 
      group_by(stock_id) %>% 
      summarise(CAR_0_3 = sum(AR), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "stock_id"
  ) %>% 
  # add chip dependency
  left_join(df %>% select(stock_id, !!chip_var) %>% distinct(),
            by = "stock_id")

# 5. Average treatment effect (pooled) ---------------------------------------
pooled_car <- mean(car_tbl$CAR_0_5)
cat("\nAverage CAR[0,5] across 80 firms:", round(pooled_car, 4), "\n")

# 6. Cross-sectional regression ----------------------------------------------
form <- as.formula(paste0("CAR_0_5 ~ ", chip_var))
cs_mod  <- lm(form, data = car_tbl)
cs_rob  <- coeftest(cs_mod, vcov = vcovHC(cs_mod, type = "HC1"))

cat("\nCross-sectional regression (robust SE):\n")
print(cs_rob)

# 7. Robustness checks --------------------------------------------------------
# (a) CAR[0,3] as dependent variable
form_alt <- as.formula(paste0("CAR_0_3 ~ ", chip_var))
cs_mod_alt <- lm(form_alt, data = car_tbl)
cs_rob_alt <- coeftest(cs_mod_alt, vcov = vcovHC(cs_mod_alt, type = "HC1"))

cat("\nRobustness: Using CAR[0,3]\n")
print(cs_rob_alt)

# (b) Market-adjusted model (AR = ret - mkt_ret) ------------------------------
df_ma <- df %>% 
  mutate(AR_ma = ret - mkt_ret)

car_ma <- df_ma %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% event_win) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  summarise(CAR_ma = sum(AR_ma), .groups = "drop") %>% 
  left_join(df %>% select(stock_id, !!chip_var) %>% distinct(),
            by = "stock_id")

form_ma <- as.formula(paste0("CAR_ma ~ ", chip_var))
cs_ma  <- lm(form_ma, data = car_ma)
cs_ma_rob <- coeftest(cs_ma, vcov = vcovHC(cs_ma, type = "HC1"))

cat("\nRobustness: Market-adjusted model\n")
print(cs_ma_rob)
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Negative.  
Reasoning: Automakers rely heavily on semiconductors; a publicised shortage should lower expected future production and profits, creating downward price pressure.  

Magnitude:  
• Average CAR[0,5] ≈ –4 % to –6 %.  
• Cross-sectional slope: a one-standard-deviation increase in chip dependency should make CAR roughly 1½–2 pp more negative (regression coefficient ≈ –0.02 to –0.03 if dependency scaled 0–1).

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study + cross-sectional CAR regression on firm-level exposure variable
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Auto stocks decline; higher chip-dependency → larger CAR loss
